teams.heading: Fiji surrender Pacific Nations Cup title to Japan following costly mistakes
teams.body: The Flying Fijians surrendered their Pacific Nations Cup crown in Tokyo on Saturday, falling 20-15 to Japan in the final. Despite leading 12-10 at half-time through tries from Virimi Vakatawa and captain Tevita Ikanivere, Senirusi Seruvakula's side crumbled after the break. Fiji paid the price for a mounting error count, finishing the match with just 36 per cent possession, 14 conceded penalties, and 24 missed tackles. Halfback Frank Lomani lamented the performance, admitting second-half mistakes let the hosts back into the contest.

lead.why: It covers the major match result where Fiji surrendered their Pacific Nations Cup title to Japan.

teams.heading: Canada end England women's historic 39-match winning streak with draw
teams.body: England women saw their historic 39-match winning run come to a dramatic end after being held to a 26-26 draw by Canada at Sandy Park in Saturday's thrilling clash. John Mitchell's side twice fell behind in a relentless first half but fought back through a Claudia Moloney-MacDonald brace and tries from Hannah Botterman and Bryony Field. Despite the draw extending their unbeaten run to 40 Tests, the Red Roses missed late chances to convert sustained pressure and must now prepare to face New Zealand.

teams.heading: Pauline Bourdon Sansus leads France women to miracle comeback against Australia
teams.body: France women staged a miraculous recovery to defeat Australia 29-26 on Saturday in Aix-en-Provence. The Test was delayed by a burning bus adjacent to the stadium and saw the hosts reduced to 11 players during the first half following four disciplinary cards. Despite trailing 19-0 and receiving six cards in total — including a 20-minute red — the French side scored 17 unanswered points in the final 25 minutes to snatch an unlikely victory.

lead.why: A 19-point comeback while playing with only 11 players due to disciplinary cards, coupled with a burning bus delay, is an extraordinary match story.

teams.heading: Ireland women surrender nineteen-point lead in WXV defeat against United States
teams.body: The Ireland women’s team suffered a frustrating 40-36 defeat to the United States in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium. Despite a dominant start that saw Scott Bemand’s side establish a 31-12 lead, a second-half loss of discipline and numerical disadvantage proved costly. Bemand admitted the side was left disappointed, noting that it was "a game we should have won." Ireland now turns its focus to upcoming fixtures against Japan, with Bemand emphasising the need for complete 80-minute performances.

teams.heading: Italy women dominate Japan to secure emphatic WXV Global Series win
teams.body: The Italy women’s side opened their WXV Global Series campaign with a resounding 55-21 victory over Japan at Stadio Omero Tognon. The Azzurre demonstrated clinical finishing throughout, with notable scores from Aura Muzzo, Alessandra Frangipani, Alyssa D'Inca, Vittoria Vecchini, and Giordana Duca. Captain Vittoria Ostuni Minuzzi marked her 50th cap with a try as the team racked up their highest-ever score against the Sakura XV, maintaining total control across the park in a comprehensive performance.

teams.heading: Scotland women suffer heavy defeat against clinical New Zealand in Edinburgh
teams.body: Scotland’s women suffered a 66-14 defeat to New Zealand at Hive Stadium on Friday. Despite two first-half tries from Evie Gallagher, the Scots struggled to contain a clinical Black Ferns side that ran in 10 tries over the 80 minutes. The result marks a second successive loss for the hosts in the WXV Global Series following their opening defeat to Canada. Scotland now turn their focus to next Saturday’s fixture, where they will host Australia at the same venue.

teams.heading: Wales women deliver eight-try performance in stunning victory over South Africa
teams.body: Wales women’s side marked a new era with an emphatic 50-19 victory over South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park. Sean Lynn’s squad showcased a revitalised attacking identity, with Sisilia Tuipulotu scoring twice and co-captain Alex Callender earning player of the match honours. After a period of development, Lynn remains focused on the long term, stating: “This is just the start for us, this is going to be our new DNA.” The result secures a strong opening to their WXV Global Series campaign.

teams.heading: Jacques Nienaber remains coy regarding his future amid Argentina coaching vacancy
teams.body: The search for a permanent Los Pumas head coach continues to revolve around Jacques Nienaber, who remains uncommitted regarding his future at Leinster. While recent reports have linked the South African to the Argentine post, he has declined to provide a concrete update on his long-term plans. Nienaber has recently focused his public remarks on his coaching philosophy and admiration for other figures in the game, leaving the UAR’s marquee target currently unconfirmed as the union pursues its permanent appointment.

teams.heading: Jordan Petaia returns to Wallabies squad for Springboks Test in Perth
teams.body: Jordan Petaia has been recalled to the Australia squad for next weekend’s one-off Test against South Africa. The utility back, who recently joined Urayasu D-Rocks, was named in Les Kiss’ 34-man group following a stint in the NFL. Petaia revealed his American football dream was curtailed by a misdiagnosed hamstring injury, but he is now targeting a place in the squad for the 2027 World Cup. Australia enters the fixture aiming to build on a recent unbeaten run.

teams.heading: Japan defeat Fiji to claim their first Pacific Nations Cup title
teams.body: Japan secured their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019 with a hard-fought 20-15 victory over Fiji at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium. After trailing by two points at half-time, the Brave Blossoms overcame the physical threat of the defending champions through tries from Mamoru Harada, Ben Gunter and Samisoni Tua. Captain Naoto Saito, named player of the tournament, described the win as a "great breakthrough" that provides this young squad with the confidence to build toward the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

teams.heading: Ardie Savea faces lengthy sideline spell following necessary shoulder surgery
teams.body: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea is set for an extended period on the sidelines after New Zealand Rugby confirmed he requires surgery on a dislocated shoulder. Sustained during the third Test against the Springboks, the injury ruled Savea out of the final series match and will keep him out of the upcoming Bledisloe Cup fixtures. While his return-to-play timeline remains unconfirmed, rehabilitation for this procedure typically requires around six months, casting significant doubt over his availability for the end-of-year Nations Championship.

lead.why: The announcement of a lengthy injury layoff for the All Blacks captain is a significant blow to the squad ahead of the upcoming fixtures.

teams.body: Coach Rassie Erasmus has sent Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende home to South Africa ahead of next weekend’s one-off Test against the Wallabies. Both first-choice players are being rested following their heavy workload during the recent series against the All Blacks. Rassie confirmed that he is comfortable with the depth available in the travelling squad to cover these absences, noting that the upcoming Test in Perth is a “massive” encounter for his side.
